title: Check yourself: What each platform lacks, where it runs and what it costs

questions.stem: A team on Amazon Bedrock plans nightly bulk jobs through the Message Batches API at half price. What do the docs say?

options.text: The endpoint works there, at the same half price as the direct API itself
options.says: Ruled out because that same list names "API endpoints (Message Batches, Models, Admin, Compliance, Usage and Cost)" as missing.

options.text: That endpoint is not offered there, so the discount route is unavailable
options.says: The Bedrock page lists "API endpoints (Message Batches, Models, Admin, Compliance, Usage and Cost)" under features not supported.

options.text: The endpoint works there, but at a ten percent premium for the region
options.says: Ruled out because the premium belongs to regional routing: "Regional endpoints carry a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints."

options.text: The endpoint works there once the Files API has been enabled first
options.says: Ruled out because the Files API is itself on the list: "URL sources for images and documents, Files API".

questions.stem: A company needs single-region data residency for Claude on Google Cloud and also wants provisioned throughput. Which type of address fits?

options.text: Any kind, since the premium buys residency on all three of them
options.says: Ruled out because "Global endpoints: Dynamic routing for maximum availability", with "No pricing premium" and no residency choice.

options.text: The global kind, since it routes to wherever capacity is free today
options.says: Ruled out because the global kind "only supports pay-as-you-go traffic (provisioned throughput requires regional endpoints)".

options.text: The multi-region kind, since it supports provisioned throughput as well
options.says: Ruled out because the multi-region kind also "supports pay-as-you-go traffic only".

options.text: The regional kind, which is required for both aims and costs 10% more
options.says: The page says regional endpoints are "Required for single-region data residency, strict compliance mandates, or provisioned throughput", at the premium.

origin.section: Where it runs: endpoints and price

questions.stem: A team must pick between the two cloud platforms and needs structured outputs and web search from it. What do the pages show?

options.text: AWS offers web search but not structured outputs, while Google's service lacks web search
options.says: Ruled out because Bedrock's list has "Server-side tools (code execution, web search, web fetch, advisor)" as missing.

options.text: AWS lacks both, while Google's service offers both
options.says: The Bedrock list has "Server-side tools (code execution, web search, web fetch, advisor)" and structured outputs among the gaps, and the Google Cloud page lists "Structured outputs" and the "Web search tool" among its supported feature highlights.

options.text: Both platforms offer both features without any exception at all
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: Bedrock lacks "Server-side tools (code execution, web search, web fetch, advisor)".

options.text: Google's service offers structured outputs but lacks web search
options.says: Ruled out because the Google Cloud page lists them "among its supported feature highlights".
